tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when...'), focuses on user intent/symptoms (call fails with access/validation/throttling error, nobody can see what the model is doing, is Bedrock set up correctly), explicitly covers trigger contexts even when the user doesn't name the domain by terms (logging, IAM, SCP, marketplace), and is a concise paragraph.
tests.evidence: Use this skill when a Bedrock call fails with an access, validation or throttling error, when nobody can see what the model is doing, or when someone asks whether Bedrock is set up correctly, even if they do not mention logging, IAM, service control policies or marketplace subscriptions by name.

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body jumps directly into domain-specific procedures (LLM-INV check catalog, API quirks, access diagnosis) without explaining general AWS/Bedrock concepts the agent would already know. It assumes familiarity with IAM, SCPs, and Bedrock APIs and focuses on project-specific conventions.
tests.evidence: You review an Amazon Bedrock deployment for configuration correctness and access, and render a posture report.

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: The body contains a check-id summary table (severity/pillar/what-it-catches) which is a compact index, not detailed reference data; the actual detection rules, remediations, and citations live in references/checks-model-invocation.md. The router table is also a thin index pointing to reference files rather than embedding full content.
tests.evidence: Full detection rules, remediations, and citations: `references/checks-model-invocation.md`.

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: All four reference files are linked with markdown link syntax in the body (Router table, Appendix, Error Handling section).
tests.evidence: `references/collection-reference.md`, `references/checks-model-invocation.md`, `references/metrics-and-logs.md`, `references/api-quirks.md` all appear as markdown links e.g. '[Model invocation logging]' is a doc link but file links like 'references/api-quirks.md' appear in Error Handling section text without brackets in some places.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: References specify when to load each file, e.g. tied to specific operator questions in the router table and specific error conditions in Error Handling section.
tests.evidence: Is my bedrock set up correctly, is invocation logging on | ... | `references/checks-model-invocation.md` (LLM-INV-001, 005, 010)

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All references use relative paths from skill root with the references/ prefix, no absolute paths or traversals.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile operations (IAM vs SCP deny distinction, logging empty-response interpretation) are given exact prescriptive guidance, while flexible areas (how to review invocation patterns) are described more loosely with rationale.
tests.evidence: An SCP deny overrides every account-level IAM allow... do NOT prescribe an IAM fix. Escalate to the org admin with the specific SCP policy name and deny statement (LLM-INV-015).

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: The skill doesn't present competing tool choices as a menu; it specifies exact APIs to call for each situation rather than listing alternative tools without a default.
tests.evidence: First read: `GetModelInvocationLoggingConfiguration`, treating empty as disabled

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The review procedure is a generalizable approach (region/account scoping, enumerate models, check IAM, diagnose access, review patterns, assemble findings) applicable to any Bedrock account review, not a one-off declaration.
tests.evidence: Run the LLM-INV family against the account under review in the target region. Work the steps in order and track progress against this checklist.

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill has an explicit 'Common wrong answers' section documenting non-obvious pitfalls like empty logging config meaning disabled, listed-vs-accessible model confusion, and inference-profile prefix misunderstanding.
tests.evidence: "The inference-profile id starts with `us.`, so it is pinned to one region." The `us.`/`eu.`/`apac.` prefix is geographic routing scope, not a region pin

tests.reasoning: The skill produces a structured posture report and does provide a template reference, satisfying the need for structured output guidance.
tests.evidence: When a full report is requested, the output follows `assets/bedrock-configuration-report-template.md`.

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body

tests.evidence: When a full report is requested, the output follows `assets/bedrock-configuration-report-template.md`.
